class: Receipt wording the shared definition missed: 'Application was successfully submitted' (Ashby) and bare 'Application has been sent' / 'Application was sent' (the probe's old list)
fix: One new _CORE alternative for the bare-application-with-auxiliary form; SubmissionProbe.inspect reads blocks through says_received (same 400-char cap as the waiting check) instead of its own twelve-phrase substring list; the eleven dead sites/*.py confirmation_phrases tuples (read by nothing) are deleted. Loose entries ('thank you for your interest' alone, 'already applied', 'your journey with') correctly stay NOT receipts and are pinned.
prevention: New receipt wording goes into confirmation_text._CORE with a says_received test; the no-adapter-list test fails any new fork.
root_cause: f297 moved the waiting check onto confirmation_text.says_received but left the job-site modules and the submission guard's probe on their own lists; comparing them showed the shared definition missed unambiguous past-tense receipts those lists knew.
symptom: An Ashby-style receipt ('Application was successfully submitted') was not read as a receipt by the waiting check, and the probe matched loose status fragments ('date applied') no other reader accepted.
why_tests_missed: The f297 receipt suite covered the wordings known then; the leftover lists were never diffed against the shared definition.
